cards.prose: Moses' seat was not invented by the Pharisees. Here a case too hard for the local judges goes up to the priests and the judge, and a verse later the sentence to be done is *according to the sentence of the law which they shall teach thee* (Deuteronomy 17:11). That is why Yahusha (Jesus) can say to observe what they bid: what is read from the seat is Moses, and the fault lies in their works.
cards.member_phrase: then shalt thou arise, and get thee up into the place which Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) shall choose
cards.member_sentence: A matter too hard for the local court goes up to the priests and the judge at the place Yahuah (the LORD) chooses, and what they teach from the law is done.

cards.prose: Malachi says what the seat is for. The priest's lips *should keep knowledge*, and the people *seek the law at his mouth*, since the priest stands as a messenger for Yahuah (the LORD) of hosts. The next verse turns on priests who *caused many to stumble at the law* (Malachi 2:8), the same line Yahusha (Jesus) draws between the law read from the seat and the works of the men sitting in it.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: The priest's lips are to keep knowledge so that the people seek the law at his mouth, which is what the seat of Moses is for.

cards.prose: The heavy burdens in this verse are the weight men stacked up and would not touch themselves, and here Yahusha (Jesus) calls the ones who are *heavy laden* to come to him for rest. What he lifts is what was laid on top, and a few verses on he says of his own yoke, *my yoke is easy, and my burden is light* (Matthew 11:30).
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: He calls the weary and heavy laden to himself for rest, the opposite of the heavy burdens bound on men's shoulders from the seat.

cards.prose: Peter's *yoke* is what the seat laid on shoulders, a price at the door: *Except ye be circumcised after the manner of Moses, ye cannot be saved* (Acts 15:1). He does not call the Torah unbearable, since the Torah is what the fathers lived by and what is read from the seat. He means the rule that nobody is in until the rite is done.
cards.member_phrase: to put a yoke upon the neck of the disciples, which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear
cards.member_sentence: Peter says the yoke put on the disciples' necks was one that neither the fathers nor the apostles were able to bear.

cards.prose: The sign on the hand and the memorial between the eyes are commanded, *that the LORD’S law may be in thy mouth*. Yahusha (Jesus) does not say to leave them off. What he marks is that they *make broad their phylacteries* to be seen, which turns something meant to keep the law in the mouth into something to be looked at.
cards.member_phrase: And it shall be for a sign unto thee upon thine hand, and for a memorial between thine eyes
cards.member_sentence: The sign on the hand and the memorial between the eyes are Yahuah's (the LORD's) own commandment, given so that his law is in the mouth.

cards.prose: Exodus says it twice, here as *a token upon thine hand, and for frontlets between thine eyes*, and each time the reason is the same, that Yahuah (the LORD) brought them out of Egypt. It is a reminder of what he did. When the Pharisees make theirs broad to be noticed, they turn a remembrance into a show, and the show is what Yahusha (Jesus) names.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: The token on the hand and the frontlets between the eyes are given to remember that Yahuah (the LORD) brought Yashar'el (Israel) out of Egypt.

cards.prose: The border is a commandment too: *make them fringes in the borders of their garments*, throughout their generations, with a ribband of blue. Yahusha (Jesus) wore one himself, so the fault he names is the habit of the Pharisees to *enlarge the borders* to be seen, and not the fringe.
cards.member_phrase: that they make them fringes in the borders of their garments throughout their generations
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) commands fringes in the borders of the garments with a ribband of blue, throughout every generation.

cards.prose: Moses puts the fringe on the garment a second time, *upon the four quarters of thy vesture*, so it is a plain commandment for everyone who wears a cloak and not a badge for a few. What Yahusha (Jesus) faults is making the border larger for men to admire, not the fringe itself.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Fringes go on the four quarters of the vesture, so the border is the Torah's own commandment and not a Pharisee's invention.

cards.prose: The woman who *touched the hem of his garment* touched the border where the commanded fringe hung, which shows Yahusha (Jesus) wore it himself. So when he says the Pharisees *enlarge the borders of their garments*, he cannot be faulting the border. The fault is the size of it and the reason for it.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: The woman touched the hem of his garment, the border where the commanded fringe hung, which shows he wore it himself.

cards.prose: Again the hem of his garment, and again people reaching for it: *as many as touched were made perfectly whole*. He wore the border and the sick took hold of it. What he names in the Pharisees is the enlarging for show, which tells you the border itself was never the woe.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Many took hold of the hem of his garment and were made perfectly whole, so the border he wore was never what the woe was against.

cards.prose: Isaiah's people say it when even the fathers cannot help them: *though Abraham be ignorant of us*, still *thou, O Yahuah (LORD), art our father*. That stands behind what Yahusha (Jesus) says to the crowd, one Master and all of them brothers, and in the very next verse one Father in heaven.
cards.member_phrase: thou, O Yahuah (LORD), art our father, our redeemer
cards.member_sentence: Even if Abraham does not know them, the people say Yahuah (the LORD) is their father and their redeemer, so the Father alone is Father.

cards.prose: *We are the clay, and thou our potter*, Isaiah says, and *we all are the work of thy hand*. Everyone made by the one hand stands level, which is why Yahusha (Jesus) can say *all ye are brethren* and leave only one Master over them.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: The people are the clay and Yahuah (the LORD) is the potter, so all are the work of one hand and none stands over the rest as father.

cards.prose: *Is not he thy father that hath bought thee?* Moses asks a people that had forgotten. The one who made them and established them is called Father there, which is why Yahusha (Jesus) leaves them one Master, calls them all brethren, and names one Father in heaven.
cards.member_phrase: is not he thy father that hath bought thee? hath he not made thee, and established thee
cards.member_sentence: Moses calls Yahuah (the LORD) the father who bought, made and established the people, so fatherhood in Yashar'el (Israel) belongs to him.

cards.prose: Paul takes no title here. They have *ten thousand instructers*, he says, but not many fathers, and the only fatherhood he claims is that *I have begotten you through the gospel*, a bringing to birth he did among them and no rank he wears over them. That is the opposite of men loving to be called Rabbi.
cards.member_phrase: yet have ye not many fathers: for in HaMashiach Yahusha (Christ Jesus) I have begotten you through the gospel
cards.member_sentence: Paul claims no title, only that he begot them through the gospel, while they have ten thousand instructers and not many fathers.

cards.prose: The question the seat answers with chief places is the one the disciples ask themselves here, *Who is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven?* Yahusha (Jesus) sets a little child in the middle: *Whosoever therefore shall humble himself as this little child, the same is greatest in the kingdom of heaven* (Matthew 18:4). That is the same low road as *he that is greatest among you shall be your servant*.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: The disciples ask who is greatest in the kingdom, and he sets a little child among them, the same low road as the servant who is greatest.

cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) sets two ways of ruling side by side. The *princes of the Gentiles exercise dominion*, and then he says *But it shall not be so among you* (Matthew 20:26). The love of chief seats is the way of those princes, and the kingdom runs the other way, where the one who is greatest is the servant.
cards.member_phrase: Ye know that the princes of the Gentiles exercise dominion over them, and they that are great exercise authority upon them
cards.member_sentence: He sets the way of the princes of the Gentiles, who exercise dominion, against the way among his own, where the great one is the servant.

cards.prose: James gives the reason behind the servant's greatness: *Elohim (God) resisteth the proud, but giveth grace unto the humble*. It is the same turn Yahusha (Jesus) names in the next verse, *whosoever shall exalt himself shall be abased; and he that shall humble himself shall be exalted* (Matthew 23:12), and James says whose hand does the turning.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Elohim (God) resists the proud and gives grace to the humble, which names who does the abasing and the exalting.

cards.prose: James gives the other half of the servant's greatness. The lifting is not taken but given, *he shall lift you up*, and it is done in the sight of Yahuah (the LORD) and not before men watching the chief seats. The servant stays low and the one who sees him raises him.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: The humble are lifted up by Yahuah (the Lord) in his own sight, so greatness for the servant is given and not seized.

cards.prose: Peter shows the servant's rule in a house with elders and younger. The younger submit to the elder, yet *all of you be subject one to another*, and all are to be *clothed with humility*. Greatness there is wearing humility, since Elohim (God) *resisteth the proud*.
cards.member_phrase: Yea, all of you be subject one to another, and be clothed with humility
cards.member_sentence: Everyone in the house is to be subject to one another and clothed with humility, because Elohim (God) resists the proud.

cards.prose: Luke gives this woe to the lawyers: *ye have taken away the key of knowledge*. Matthew's shut door and Luke's missing key are one charge, that the ones who sat over the people neither went in themselves nor let those who were *entering in* through, and it is the people who pay for it.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Luke tells the same woe as taking away the key of knowledge, so those who sat over the people neither entered nor let others enter.

cards.prose: Paul's *another gospel* is the one the woe describes at work, sea and land crossed to make a proselyte and the proselyte told that joining is what saves him. The agitators carried that to Galatia, and Paul marvels that the people there were so soon moved from *him that called you* to it.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Paul marvels that the Galatians were so soon turned from the one who called them to another gospel, the proselyte-maker's gospel.

cards.prose: Paul's *who hath bewitched you* is aimed at the pull the woe describes, the claim that a rite and a membership put a person in. The Galatians had already seen Yahusha (Jesus) *evidently set forth, crucified among you*, and what was turning them from *obey the truth* was a gospel that said joining would save them.
cards.member_phrase: who hath bewitched you, that ye should not obey the truth
cards.member_sentence: Paul asks who bewitched the Galatians away from obeying the truth, when Yahusha (Jesus) had been set forth crucified before their eyes.

cards.prose: The proselyte's bargain, said flat: *Except ye be circumcised*, *ye cannot be saved*. It is said to brothers already counted in, and it is the same price of entry the woe describes. The man made over to it ends up what Yahusha (Jesus) calls *twofold more the child of hell* than the ones who made him.
cards.member_phrase: taught the brethren, and said, Except ye be circumcised after the manner of Moses, ye cannot be saved
cards.member_sentence: Men from Judæa teach the brethren that without circumcision they cannot be saved, the same price of entry the proselyte-makers charged.

cards.prose: Pharisees who had believed bring the old habit into the assembly: *it was needful to circumcise them*, as if the rite were the door. The law of Moses is not the fault. The fault is the order, the rite first and then you are in, which makes a man what the woe calls *twofold more the child of hell*.
cards.member_phrase: certain of the sect of the Pharisees which believed, saying, That it was needful to circumcise them
cards.member_sentence: Believing Pharisees insist the brothers must be circumcised, making the rite the door in, the same gospel the proselyte-makers carried.

cards.prose: The *yoke* Peter names is the proselyte's yoke, being made one of them by the rite and counted saved for it. He says *neither our fathers nor we were able to bear* it, and he does not mean the Torah, since the fathers lived by the Torah and the seat reads from it. He means the system made out of it.
cards.member_phrase: to put a yoke upon the neck of the disciples, which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear
cards.member_sentence: Peter's yoke is the proselyte's price of entry, which neither the fathers nor the apostles could carry, and it is not the Torah itself.

cards.prose: Here the oath is set down first as a commandment: *shalt perform unto Yahuah (Lord) thine oaths*. That is the line the blind guides step around. A man who swears by the gold or the gift and calls the other oath *it is nothing* has found a way out of performing what he swore.
cards.member_phrase: Thou shalt not forswear thyself, but shalt perform unto Yahuah (Lord) thine oaths
cards.member_sentence: The oath is a commandment to perform, so any way of swearing that frees a man from what he swore has already left the commandment.
cards.flag: The old note quoted 'Swear not at all' (the verse after this one); the pair points at 5:33, so I wrote on the commandment to perform oaths.

cards.prose: The commandment about oaths rests on the name: *ye shall not swear by my name falsely*, and the verse closes with *I am Yahuah (LORD)*. That is why the answer to the gold and the gift traces every oath upward: *whoso shall swear by the temple, sweareth by it, and by him that dwelleth therein* (Matthew 23:21). No oath stops short of the one it is sworn before.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Oaths rest on the name of Yahuah (the LORD), so swearing by it falsely profanes it and no oath can be sorted into one that is nothing.

cards.prose: Numbers puts it without an exception: *he shall not break his word*, and he is held to *all that proceedeth out of his mouth*. A system that sorts oaths into the ones that bind and the ones where *it is nothing* has made exceptions the commandment never made.
cards.member_phrase: he shall not break his word, he shall do according to all that proceedeth out of his mouth
cards.member_sentence: A man who vows or swears is bound by all that comes out of his mouth, with no oath sorted out as nothing.

cards.prose: *Thou shalt not slack to pay it*, Moses says, and an unpaid vow *would be sin in thee*. Calling an oath by the temple *it is nothing* and one by the gold a debt only moves the debt around, because Yahuah (the LORD) *will surely require it of thee*.
cards.member_phrase: thou shalt not slack to pay it: for Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) will surely require it of thee; and it would be sin in thee
cards.member_sentence: A vow made to Yahuah (the LORD) must be paid, and he will require it, so no vow is excused by the thing it was sworn on.

cards.prose: James lands where the woe ends: *he that shall swear by heaven, sweareth by the throne of Elohim (God), and by him that sitteth thereon* (Matthew 23:22). So James can say *neither by heaven*, and ask only for a plain word, *let your yea be yea; and your nay, nay*. A word that is simply kept leaves no use for graded oaths.
cards.member_phrase: let your yea be yea; and your nay, nay; lest ye fall into condemnation
cards.member_sentence: James takes away every oath by heaven or earth and asks for a plain yea and nay, the same end the woe reaches.

cards.prose: Micah had already said what Yahuah (the LORD) requires, and it is the same list: *to do justly, and to love mercy*. Yahusha (Jesus) names judgment and mercy as the weightier matters, then adds *not to leave the other undone*, so the tithe stays. Micah's *walk humbly with thy Elohim (God)* sits beside the mint, not in place of it.
cards.member_phrase: to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy Elohim (God)
cards.member_sentence: Micah says what Yahuah (the LORD) requires, justice, mercy and a humble walk with Elohim (God), the same weightier matters the woe names.

cards.prose: Hosea's *I desired mercy, and not sacrifice* weighs the two against each other and does not cancel the altar. Sacrifice was commanded and went on. What Yahuah (the LORD) wanted along with it was mercy and *the knowledge of Elohim (God)*, the same order Yahusha (Jesus) keeps with *these ought ye to have done, and not to leave the other undone*.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) desired mercy and the knowledge of Elohim (God) more than burnt offerings, which weighs what the offering stands for.

cards.prose: Isaiah's Yahuah (the LORD) is *full of the burnt offerings of rams*, and the speech opens *give ear unto the law of our Elohim (God)* (Isaiah 1:10), so the law is not what is refused. What he will not take is the full count of offerings from rulers who have left out what the law weighs more heavily, as the Pharisees *omitted* judgment and mercy.
cards.member_phrase: To what purpose is the multitude of your sacrifices unto me? saith Yahuah (LORD): I am full of the burnt offerings of rams
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) is full of burnt offerings from rulers who left justice undone, so the count of sacrifices does not answer what he asked.
cards.flag: The old note quoted Isaiah 1:16-17, but the pair points at 1:11; I used 1:10 from the context to show the law is not what is refused.

cards.prose: Yahuah (the LORD) hates the feast days here because of what stands a few verses later: *let judgment run down as waters, and righteousness as a mighty stream* (Amos 5:24). The feasts are his own appointments, so the complaint is that they were kept while the weightier part was left alone, as the mint was counted and judgment *omitted*.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) despises feast days kept without judgment and righteousness, the appointed part carried out and the weightier part left.
cards.flag: The old note quoted Amos 5:24, but the pair points at 5:21; I brought 5:24 in from the context.

cards.prose: The verse itself only says the word of Yahuah (the LORD) came to Zechariah, and the word that follows is the one Yahusha (Jesus) is pointing at: *Execute true judgment, and shew mercy and compassions every man to his brother* (Zechariah 7:9). Judgment and mercy are the weightier matters spoken by the prophets before him, and the mint stays beside them.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: The word of Yahuah (the LORD) comes to Zechariah, and what follows in the next verse is judgment and mercy shown every man to his brother.
cards.flag: The old note meant 7:9 (the content of the word), but the pair points at 7:8, which is only the introduction; I quoted 7:9 as the verse that follows.

cards.prose: Here is the tithe the Pharisees paid down to the herbs, and it is a commandment: *Thou shalt truly tithe*. Yahusha (Jesus) does not touch it. He says *these ought ye to have done*, and faults them only for leaving the weightier matters undone beside it.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: The tithe of the increase of the field is Torah's own commandment, which the woe leaves standing.

cards.prose: The tithe is called *holy unto Yahuah (LORD)*, so a man who tithes mint and anise and cummin is handling something set apart, and the woe does not ask him to stop. It asks that he not stop there, since the same Yahuah (the LORD) asks for judgment, mercy and faith. *Not to leave the other undone* means both stand together.
cards.member_phrase: is the LORD’S: it is holy unto Yahuah (LORD)
cards.member_sentence: The tithe of the land is holy to Yahuah (the LORD), so tithing mint and cummin is not the fault the woe names.

cards.prose: He calls the multitude to *Hear, and understand*, and what he teaches is the cup turned inside out: *that which cometh out of the mouth, this defileth a man* (Matthew 15:11). A man can scrub the *outside of the cup and of the platter* all day, and what is *within* is what he is carrying.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: He calls the multitude to hear and understand that what comes out of a man defiles him, which turns the cup's outside to its inside.

cards.prose: Mark opens the same fight with Pharisees and scribes who *came from Jerusalem* to find fault over unwashed hands, and a few verses on names *the washing of cups, and pots, brasen vessels* (Mark 7:4). That is the cup and platter of the woe, a tradition of cleaning the outside of vessels while the inside went unwashed.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Pharisees and scribes come down from Jerusalem to find fault over washing, the tradition of clean vessels that the cup and platter woe answers.

cards.prose: This is the real uncleanness the paint covers: whoever touches the dead body *shall be unclean seven days*. Yahusha (Jesus) says the men in the seat are like whited tombs *full of dead men’s bones, and of all uncleanness*, so what looked beautiful outside is the very thing the law says defiles, and nobody walking past was warned.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Whoever touches a dead body is unclean seven days, the uncleanness the whited tombs hid under paint.

cards.prose: The wall *daubed it with untempered morter* is the same trick as the whited tomb, a coat that makes something look sound over what is not. Ezekiel's prophets cried *Peace; and there was no peace*, and Yahusha (Jesus) says the tombs *appear beautiful outward*. In Ezekiel the daubed wall comes down: *that it shall fall* (Ezekiel 13:11).
cards.member_phrase: one built up a wall, and, lo, others daubed it with untempered morter
cards.member_sentence: A wall daubed with untempered morter over false peace is the whitewash on a tomb, a coat that hides what is not sound.

cards.prose: In Jeremiah, Yahuah (the LORD) has been sending *all my servants the prophets*, *daily rising up early*, since the day the fathers left Egypt. The woe is the long end of that sending, with men now building the tombs of the prophets who were refused. The sending is the same one, and only the tombs are new.
cards.member_phrase: I have even sent unto you all my servants the prophets, daily rising up early and sending them
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) sent all his servants the prophets daily since Egypt, the same sending the tomb-builders now honor after the fact.

cards.prose: *But ye have not hearkened*, Jeremiah says of the prophets Yahuah (the LORD) sent, and Yahusha (Jesus) says the ones who *garnish the sepulchres of the righteous* were not listening either. A decorated tomb honors a prophet who is dead. The question put to Jeremiah's hearers was whether the living one was heard.
cards.member_phrase: all his servants the prophets, rising early and sending them; but ye have not hearkened, nor inclined your ear to hear
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) sent all his servants the prophets and they were not heard, so tombs for the dead prophets answer nothing.

cards.prose: Nehemiah's confession puts two things side by side, that they *cast thy law behind their backs, and slew thy prophets*. The prophets came *to turn them to thee* and were killed for it, which is the history the builders of the tombs were standing on while saying they would have done differently.
cards.member_phrase: cast thy law behind their backs, and slew thy prophets which testified against them to turn them to thee
cards.member_sentence: The people cast the law behind their backs and slew the prophets sent to turn them back, the history the tomb-builders inherit.

cards.prose: Stephen's line to the men in front of him is the woe in short, *as your fathers did, so do ye*. Like the ones decorating the tombs of the prophets, they honor the dead ones and *resist the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit)* in the living, which makes them heirs of the fathers they say they differ from.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Stephen tells the men before him that they resist the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) as their fathers did, the pattern Yahusha (Jesus) names.

cards.prose: Here the Torah shows judgment waiting on a measure: *the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet full*, and for generations it held. The woe runs the same law from the other side, *Fill ye up then the measure of your fathers* (Matthew 23:32), the sins of the fathers carried on by those who build their tombs, until the measure is complete.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Judgment waits for a measure of iniquity to fill, which is the measure Yahusha (Jesus) tells the tomb-builders to fill up.

cards.prose: Moses sings of a judgment that is not forgotten but *laid up in store*, sealed with Yahuah (the LORD), and a verse later says why it waits: *their foot shall slide in due time* (Deuteronomy 32:35). The blood of the prophets in the woe is that kind of stored account, held until the measure is full and then asked of the generation that fills it.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Judgment is laid up in store and sealed with Yahuah (the LORD) until its time, as the blood of the prophets is held for the generation that fills the measure.

cards.prose: Paul names the same pattern a generation on. The believers in Judæa suffered from men of their own people, and he says those who killed *their own prophets* (1 Thessalonians 2:15) did it *to fill up their sins alway* (1 Thessalonians 2:16). He is a Yahudi (Jew) writing about the men persecuting, and the assemblies in Judæa were Yahudim (Jews) too, so he describes the killers, not a people.
cards.member_phrase: for ye also have suffered like things of your own countrymen, even as they have of the Yahudim (Jews)
cards.member_sentence: Paul says the believers in Judæa suffered from their own countrymen, the men who, a verse later, filled up their sins by killing the prophets.
cards.flag: This passage is easily turned against a whole people; I tied it to the men doing the killing and noted the Judæan assemblies were Yahudim (Jews) themselves.

cards.prose: John says *generation of vipers* to the *Pharisees and Sadducees* who came to his baptism, and Yahusha (Jesus) says it again to the scribes and Pharisees. Both times it falls on rulers who came with their standing, and both times it is joined to judgment, *the wrath to come* there and *the damnation of hell* here.
cards.member_phrase: he said unto them, O generation of vipers, who hath warned you to flee from the wrath to come
cards.member_sentence: John calls the Pharisees and Sadducees a generation of vipers and warns of the wrath to come, the same name and the same judgment as the woe.

cards.prose: He used the name before, with the reason attached: *how can ye, being evil, speak good things?* The words come out of what the heart is full of, and in this chapter he says what these men are full of, *within ye are full of hypocrisy and iniquity* (Matthew 23:28). The vipers are named by what comes out of them.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: The vipers are named by their speech, since out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks, the same reasoning as the inside of the cup.

cards.prose: The serpent here has a seed, and *between thy seed and her seed* is the enmity set from the garden on. When Yahusha (Jesus) calls men on the seat *serpents*, he speaks of that seed surfacing inside the covenant people among the ones in the robes, and not of the people they were devouring, who are the sheep.
cards.member_phrase: I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed
cards.member_sentence: The serpent's seed and the woman's seed are set at enmity from the garden, and the serpents in the woe are that seed surfacing among the rulers.

cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) says it to men in front of him, *Ye are of your father the devil*, and then names the works, *a murderer from the beginning*. Matthew's *serpents* and John's children of the devil are one charge, made by what they do, as the woe goes on to say they will kill the prophets he sends. It is said of particular men, not of a people.
cards.member_phrase: Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do. He was a murderer from the beginning
cards.member_sentence: He names the rulers in front of him as of their father the devil by their works, a murderer from the beginning, and not a whole people.

cards.prose: He names where the count begins, *the blood of righteous Abel* (Matthew 23:35), and here is that blood being shed: Cain *rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him*. The sending of prophets and the killing of them start in the first field, and the woe says the whole count is coming due on the ones who keep it going.
cards.member_phrase: Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him
cards.member_sentence: Cain kills Abel his brother in the field, the first of the righteous blood Yahusha (Jesus) says is coming due on this generation.

cards.prose: Matthew's Zechariah stands at the other end of the count, and this is the priest on whom the Spirit of Elohim (God) came, whose message was *Why transgress ye the commandments of Yahuah (LORD)*. The prophets were sent to press the commandments on a people who had left them, and that is what the sending and the killing both turn on.
cards.member_phrase: Thus saith Elohim (God), Why transgress ye the commandments of Yahuah (LORD), that ye cannot prosper?
cards.member_sentence: The Spirit of Elohim (God) comes on Zechariah the priest to ask why they transgress the commandments of Yahuah (the LORD), and he is the slain prophet at the end of the count.
cards.flag: Matthew says Zechariah son of Barachias, while this card ties him to Zechariah son of Jehoiada; I followed the card and did not settle the identity.

cards.prose: Matthew names *Zechariah son of Barachias* (Matthew 23:35), and here the writing prophet opens as *the son of Berechiah*, the same name in its Hebrew shape. Whether Yahusha (Jesus) means this Zechariah or the priest, Jehoiada's son, is left open on the page, and the point stands either way: the count of the slain reaches the temple and the altar.
cards.member_phrase: came the word of Yahuah (LORD) unto Zechariah, the son of Berechiah, the son of Iddo the prophet
cards.member_sentence: The writing prophet Zechariah is named the son of Berechiah, the Hebrew shape of the name Matthew gives as Barachias.
cards.flag: Two Zechariahs are candidates for the one Matthew names; nothing on the page settles which, so the card holds both in view.

cards.prose: Luke gives the saying to *the wisdom of Elohim (God)* where Matthew has Yahusha (Jesus) saying it in the first person, *I send unto you prophets*. The sender is the same voice that sent the prophets from the beginning, and the answer is the same, *some of them they shall slay and persecute*.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Luke attributes the sending of prophets and apostles, some to be slain and persecuted, to the wisdom of Elohim (God), the same sender as in Matthew.

cards.prose: Matthew's list of what is done to the sent ones, *kill and crucify*, *scourge*, and *persecute them from city to city*, is the list Hebrews gives: *They were stoned, they were sawn asunder* (Hebrews 11:37). Hebrews also says what became of them, that they refused deliverance *that they might obtain a better resurrection*, so the killing is not the last word on them.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Those tortured and slain refused deliverance that they might obtain a better resurrection, so the killing of the sent ones is not their end.
cards.flag: The old note quoted Hebrews 11:37-38; the pair points at 11:35, so I used 11:37 from the context beside it.

cards.prose: Moses sings the same picture of Yahuah (the LORD) with an eagle's wings: *spreadeth abroad her wings, taketh them, beareth them on her wings*. Yahusha (Jesus) says he would have gathered the city's children *as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings*, so he stands where Moses placed Yahuah (the LORD) over the young. It is the one who carried them then who is speaking now.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) is pictured as an eagle spreading her wings and bearing her young, the picture Yahusha (Jesus) uses over Jerusalem.

cards.prose: Boaz tells Ruth she has come *under whose wings thou art come to trust*, the wings of Yahuah (the LORD), the Elohim (God) of Yashar'el (Israel). Yahusha (Jesus) offers the same shelter to Jerusalem, gathering them *under her wings*, and says the refusal was theirs: *ye would not*.
cards.member_phrase: a full reward be given thee of Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), under whose wings thou art come to trust
cards.member_sentence: Ruth comes to trust under the wings of Yahuah (the LORD), the Elohim (God) of Yashar'el (Israel), the shelter Yahusha (Jesus) offers Jerusalem.

cards.prose: Isaiah's picture is a bird over its nest, *As birds flying*, and Yahusha (Jesus) uses the same image over the same city, wanting to gather her children under his wings. The one who promised to defend Jerusalem like that is now lamenting *ye would not*, so the desolation in the next verse reads as the defender stepping back.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) of hosts is pictured as birds flying to defend Jerusalem, the shelter the hen's wings offer in the woe.

cards.prose: Yahuah (the LORD) speaks it in Jeremiah as grief, *I have forsaken mine house*, and while the house is given up, *the dearly beloved of my soul* is still named his own. Yahusha (Jesus) says the same at the temple, *your house is left unto you desolate*, and it is the house that is left, the temple and its rule, not the people he laments.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) forsakes his house while still calling the people the dearly beloved of his soul, so the house is left and not the people.

cards.prose: The warning is conditional in Jeremiah: *if ye will not hear these words*, *this house shall become a desolation*. Yahusha (Jesus) says it now because the hearing was refused, and what is left desolate is the house, the building and the rule that sat in it.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) swears that if they will not hear, this house shall become a desolation, the sentence on the house.

cards.prose: After *your house is left unto you desolate* the next thing Matthew tells is that he walks out: *departed from the temple*. The leaving is the saying acted out, and the disciples pointing at the buildings set up his answer, *There shall not be left here one stone upon another* (Matthew 24:2).
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: He departs from the temple right after leaving the house desolate, and the disciples point at the buildings he says will come down.

cards.prose: The king of the parable answers the murder of his servants by burning *their city*. Yahusha (Jesus) says here that the house is left desolate to the men who kill the prophets he sends. The burned city and the desolate house are one judgment on the same rulers, told once in a story and once in plain speech.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: In the parable the murderers are destroyed and their city burned up, the same judgment the woe pronounces on the house.

cards.prose: The parting word is a quotation. The line from the Psalm that the crowds sang at his coming, *Blessed be he that cometh in the name of Yahuah (LORD)*, is the line he says must be said again before he is seen. The leaving is not the end of it, since the same words are to come back from the same city.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: The Psalm's blessing on him who comes in the name of Yahuah (the LORD) is what he says must be said before he is seen again.

cards.prose: Here is the crowd that said it. The multitudes before and behind *cried, saying, Hosanna to the Son of David*, and Yahusha (Jesus) says the city will not see him again until it says the blessing again. The cry was sung over him once at the gate, and the second time is the saying he waits for.
cards.member_phrase: Hosanna to the Son of David: Blessed is he that cometh in the name of Yahuah (Lord); Hosanna in the highest
cards.member_sentence: The multitudes cried Hosanna and the blessing on him who comes in the name of Yahuah (the Lord), the saying he says must come again.

cards.prose: The ones who cried it in the temple were *the children crying in the temple*, and the chief priests and scribes were *sore displeased*. The men who will not say *Blessed is he that cometh* are the kind who objected when the children said it, and Yahusha (Jesus) says it will be said by them yet.
cards.member_phrase: the children crying in the temple, and saying, Hosanna to the Son of David; they were sore displeased
cards.member_sentence: Children cry Hosanna in the temple while the chief priests and scribes are sore displeased, the saying he says must come from them yet.

cards.prose: The *till* in this verse has its day here. When Yahuah (the LORD) pours out *the spirit of grace and of supplications* on Jerusalem, *they shall look upon me whom they have pierced*, and mourn as for an only son. That looking is the seeing he says is withheld until they say the blessing.
cards.member_phrase: they shall look upon me whom they have pierced, and they shall mourn for him, as one mourneth for his only son
cards.member_sentence: When the spirit of grace and supplications is poured out, they look upon the one they pierced and mourn, the seeing held back until the blessing is said.

cards.prose: The sorting runs ahead of the return. *Two parts therein shall be cut off and die*, and *the third shall be left therein*. The next verse says *I will bring the third part through the fire, and will refine them as silver is refined* (Zechariah 13:9), and that *they shall call on my name, and I will hear them* (Zechariah 13:9). So the saying of the blessing reads as coming from a refined third, not from the whole city.
cards.member_phrase: in all the land, saith Yahuah (LORD), two parts therein shall be cut off and die; but the third shall be left therein
cards.member_sentence: Two parts of the land are cut off and a third is left, the third that is refined and calls on his name.

cards.prose: Both run on an *until*. The not-seeing in the woe lasts *till ye shall say*, and Paul's blindness lasts *until the fulness of the Gentiles be come in*, which is the scattered seed coming home, and then *all Yashar'el (Israel) shall be saved* (Romans 11:26). The house is left desolate for a time, and the end of it is a saving.
cards.member_phrase: blindness in part is happened to Yashar'el (Israel), until the fulness of the Gentiles be come in
cards.member_sentence: Blindness in part has come on Yashar'el (Israel) only until the fulness of the Gentiles comes in, the same until as the woe.
cards.flag: The old note quoted Romans 11:26; the pair points at 11:25, so I brought 11:26 in from the context.

new_threads.title: The seat of Moses and what was laid on it
new_threads.summary_md:
It ain't new. The seat the scribes and the Pharisees sit in was set up by Moses, and Yahusha (Jesus) opens the chapter by telling the crowd to honor what is read from it and to leave the works alone:

*The scribes and the Pharisees sit in Moses’ seat* (Matthew 23:2)

*All therefore whatsoever they bid you observe, that observe and do; but do not ye after their works: for they say, and do not.* (Matthew 23:3)

The seat is in the Torah. A case too hard for the local court goes up to the priests and the judge, and what they teach out of the law is what is done:

*According to the sentence of the law which they shall teach thee, and according to the judgment which they shall tell thee, thou shalt do* (Deuteronomy 17:11)

So the law read from the seat stands. The fault is in the works and in the burdens laid on top of it, loads bound on other men's shoulders by hands that would not touch them. The same goes for the signs that were commanded in the first place. The fringe, the frontlet and the title of Father were all spoken of in Moses and the prophets before the Pharisees ever sat down, so the woe is not against any of them. It is against making them larger to be seen:

*But all their works they do for to be seen of men: they make broad their phylacteries, and enlarge the borders of their garments* (Matthew 23:5)

*Speak unto the children of Yashar'el (Israel), and bid them that they make them fringes in the borders of their garments throughout their generations* (Numbers 15:38)

Yahusha (Jesus) wore the border himself, and people reached for the hem of his garment to be healed. On the title, he sends the crowd back to the Father the prophets already named:

*And call no man your father upon the earth: for one is your Father, which is in heaven.* (Matthew 23:9)

*Doubtless thou art our father, though Abraham be ignorant of us* (Isaiah 63:16)
